rationale: State-preserving handoff at the end of the available run time; no new experiment is started because the remaining interval cannot fit a validated one. Both saved candidates currently have no listed unknowns. The confirmed implementation violation is claim-config-publish-requires-durable-append, proved by direct check 3b256fe6f42b4154b75d4d2ec02e27bf (execution 452a068dbfa1488ea15bc730a0f1e7bd, checker correspondence no_issue_found, outcome violated): a leader that received a LogStore.StoreLogs error for a membership-change entry still published that configuration as configurations.latest while the assigned log index was absent from durable storage, and it could not regain leadership because its live quorum counted the unreachable voter. Supporting retained results are the follower-side negative result (exploration 6c1f4fbd37ad49e79cd922b03259d1fe), the real-producer truncation result showing the cached and reported last-log index stranded above durable content (exploration 9751d8de6e634624998aa5475f25d523), and the separate configuration-index observation (exploration 86b51caa6a8141a9802f09aa24ea13af) whose practical reach is bounded to misleading telemetry and a lost prevIndex guard for external callers, with no in-tree caller relying on it. Boundaries remain explicit and unchanged: the StoreLogs failures are injected at the real store boundary, the clusters are in-process and in-memory, and the last-log-cache divergence is a distinct observation from the confirmed published-configuration violation. Keeping candidate 70dc8f86c666457abd3005cc666d5931 active preserves both investigations, their evidence and their boundaries so a successor can pick up either the configuration-index contract or a production-backend store-error reproduction without redoing the confirmed work.
